name: PayPal Holdings, Inc.
one_line_reason: The high-margin branded PayPal button is losing ground to Apple Pay, Shop Pay and card wallets, so total volume grows while the profitable part shrinks; the board fired the CEO and dropped the 2027 targets in February 2026.
evidence: Q3 2026 revenue +2% (1% FX-neutral) to $8.58B and transaction margin dollars +2% while TPV grew 6%, i.e. growth comes from low-margin Braintree processing, not branded checkout (8-K EX-99.1, 2026-10-27). The Q3 10-Q (filed 2026-10-27) says revenue from 'PayPal products and services' fell about $240M y/y on mix and 'higher co-marketing campaigns and incentives' even as Braintree added $270M and Venmo $100M. GAAP operating income -8% and free cash flow -17% to $1.43B in Q3; active accounts +0.6% to 440M. On 2026-02-03 the board replaced CEO Alex Chriss with chair Enrique Lores and withdrew the 2027 investor-day targets; shareholders now sue over undisclosed 'impediments to its branded checkout growth strategy' (10-Q legal note).
key_numbers: P/E 9.2 vs 41.3 10y median; FCF yield 11.6% (FY2025 FCF $5.56B); shares -16% in 3y; Q3-26 rev +2%, TM$ +2%, TPV +6%; branded-products revenue -$240M y/y in Q3

name: Mastercard Incorporated
one_line_reason: Nothing is wrong and nothing is cheap: a 14%-growth card network trading at 37x earnings, slightly above its own 36x ten-year median, 4% below its all-time high.
evidence: Q3 2026 net revenue +14% to $9.8B (also +14% currency-neutral), operating margin 59.8%, diluted EPS +22% to $5.28; gross dollar volume +7%, cross-border +11%, switched transactions +9% (8-K EX-99.1, 2026-10-29). FY2025 revenue $32.8B, operating income $18.9B, FCF $17.2B (EDGAR XBRL). The stock is +62% over three years and 4.4% off its 3-year high (yfinance, 2026-11-18). It entered the toll-road list on quality; the valuation leg never fired.
key_numbers: P/E 37.5 vs 35.8 10y median; EV/EBIT 30.4 vs 28.2; P/FCF 32.7 vs 32.9; FCF yield 3.1%; ROIC 74%; Q3-26 rev +14%

name: Visa Inc.
one_line_reason: Visa just posted its fastest non-recovery growth in 15 years and the stock is near its high at 33-35x earnings and cash flow; the toll is fully priced.
evidence: FY2026 (ended 2026-09-30) net revenue +15% to $45.9B, GAAP EPS +21% to $12.32, payments volume +9%, cross-border +13%, processed transactions +9%; FY capital returned $25.6B and the dividend raised 16% (8-K EX-99.1, 2026-10-27). Q4 included a further $469M interchange-litigation (MDL) provision, a recurring cost rather than a threat to the model. Stock +70% over three years, 4.7% off its 3-year high (yfinance 2026-11-18).
key_numbers: P/E 33.0 (own 10y median not computed: Visa reports per-class EPS); P/FCF 35.1; FCF yield 2.8%; FY26 rev +15%; OM 61%

name: Coinbase Global, Inc.
one_line_reason: A crypto bear market since the October 2025 bitcoin peak cut trading volume and revenue by a third; the screen saw cheapness only because it measured the 2025 boom-year earnings.
evidence: Quarterly revenue fell from $2.03B (Q1 2025) and $1.87B (Q3 2025) to $1.41B, $1.22B and $1.22B in Q1-Q3 2026, i.e. Q3 2026 -35% y/y; GAAP net loss of $394M in Q1 and $359M in Q2 2026, then +$719M in Q3 helped by a 37% September rebound in crypto prices that flows through crypto held at fair value (XBRL, 10-Qs filed 2026-05-07, 07-30, 10-29). The Q3 deck (8-K 2026-10-29) shows market spot volume -6% q/q, volatility at multi-year lows, paid Coinbase One subscribers -24% y/y and the loan book -74% y/y, while Coinbase's own volume share rose for a fourth straight quarter to 10.7% and subscription & services reached 49% of revenue. Q3 adjusted EBITDA was $333M.
key_numbers: Trailing P/E 22.5 on FY2025 vs 38 own median, but yfinance forward P/E 45; Q3-26 rev $1.22B (-35% y/y); Q3 adj. EBITDA $333M (~$1.3B annualized vs EV $27B); shares +29% in 3y; stock -74% from 3y high

name: S&P Global Inc.
one_line_reason: A ratings-and-index toll road still growing 7-8% organically and trading at its own historical multiple; the 15% slip from the 2025 high reflects the AI worry about its desktop-data unit, which management is now preparing to sell or spin.
evidence: Q3 2026 revenue +7% to $3.678B, adjusted EPS +9% to $4.58, adjusted operating margin 53.5%; 2026 guidance organic constant-currency growth 7.5-8.5% and more than $7B of buybacks (8-K EX-99, 2026-10-27). The same release announced a strategic review, 'including potential separation', of Capital IQ and associated data businesses, the seat-based desktop product most exposed to AI substitution, while keeping Ratings and Indices. Mobility was spun off as Mobility Global (MBGL, ~$7.1B market cap) on 2026-07-01; yfinance books the spin as a 1.057 split factor, so the screen's FY2025 P/E (which still includes Mobility earnings) is only roughly comparable.
key_numbers: P/E 28.9 vs 30.4 10y median; EV/EBIT 21.6 vs 20.8; P/FCF 23.7 vs 24.3; FCF yield 4.2%; 2026 organic growth guide 7.5-8.5%; stock -15.5% from Aug-2025 high

name: MSCI Inc.

evidence: Q3 2026 operating revenue +12.4% to $892.0M (organic +12.3%), asset-based fees +24.9%, recurring subscriptions +7.7%, operating margin 56.3%, diluted EPS +14.4% to $4.86; organic subscription run-rate growth 8.7% and retention 95.0% (8-K EX-99.1, 2026-10-20). key_numbers: P/E 37.9 vs 37.1 10y median; EV/EBIT 30.3 vs 31.0; P/FCF 31.2 vs 32.3; FCF yield 3.2%; retention 95.0%; organic rev +12.3%

name: FactSet Research Systems Inc.
one_line_reason: The market priced FactSet as a seat business that AI will hollow out and punished a two-point margin reset, but users, subscription value and retention all grew in FY2026; the damage so far is cost, not demand.
evidence: FY2026 (ended 2026-08-31) organic ASV +7.0% to $2,568M, organic revenue +6.7%, ASV retention above 95% and client retention 90% (8-K EX-99.1, 2026-09-30). The 10-K (filed 2026-10-20) shows users +9.8% to 260,671 and clients +2.9% to 9,258, users driven by wealth management; subscription value per user slipped about 2.7% (my calculation, ~$10.1k to ~$9.8k) on that mix. Adjusted operating margin fell from 36.3% to 34.5% and GAAP EPS fell 6.3% to $14.57 on restructuring, incentive pay and one-time CEO awards; FY2027 guidance is organic ASV +5.0-6.5% (a slowdown) with adjusted margin 34.75-35.25%. A broker downgraded it to Sell in June 2026 on AI and Bloomberg/LSEG competition; the stock fell to ~$264 on 2026-09-30 and has since rallied to $316.67.
key_numbers: P/E 20.9 vs 30.3 10y median; P/FCF 15.8 vs 26.3; FCF yield 6.3% (FY26 FCF $708M, +14.6%); users +9.8%; ASV retention >95%; FY27 organic ASV guide 5.0-6.5%; short interest 12.6%

name: Zoetis Inc.
one_line_reason: Zoetis's pet-drug blockbusters are all being attacked at once (cheaper rival dermatology drugs, parasiticide competition, generics on Convenia and Cerenia, Librela safety doubts) while vet visits soften, so a growth franchise has turned into a shrinking one.
evidence: Q3 2026 revenue -1% to $2.4B with U.S. revenue -6% and U.S. companion animal -8%, 'reflecting macro-driven price sensitivity and competitive pressure in dermatology, as well as generic competition'; livestock +5% U.S. and +9% international offset part of it (8-K EX-99.1, 2026-11-05). The 10-Q (2026-09-30) names competitive pressure on the dermatology franchise and Simparica Trio, generic competition on Convenia and Cerenia, and lower Librela sales, and discloses a securities class action alleging the company concealed declining demand for Librela, Simparica Trio, Apoquel and Cytopoint. FY2026 revenue guidance is now $9.22-9.32B, organic -2% to -1%, below FY2025's $9.47B; the stock fell about 21% after the Q1 guidance cut in May 2026 and Elanco's Zenrelia is reportedly priced about 20% below Apoquel (news leads).
key_numbers: P/E 13.0 vs 34.0 10y median; P/FCF 15.2 vs 44.3; FCF yield 6.6%; FY26 organic revenue guide -2% to -1%; Q3 U.S. companion animal -8%; net debt $7.5B

name: Doximity, Inc.
one_line_reason: An AI-native rival (OpenEvidence) is taking doctors' attention and pharma ad dollars at lower prices, so Doximity's growth collapsed from 20%+ to 4% and it must spend heavily on AI just to defend its audience.
evidence: Q2 FY2027 (quarter to 2026-09-30) revenue +4% to $174.5M, adjusted EBITDA -12% to $88.9M (margin 50.9% vs 59.8%), net income $34.7M vs $62.1M (8-K EX-99.1, 2026-11-05). The 10-Q shows net revenue retention down to 103% from 118% a year earlier, with $500k+ customers only 124 vs 120. FY2027 revenue guide $678-683M (about +6-7% on FY2026's ~$640M). The stock fell ~24% on 2026-05-14 after FY27 guidance, with brokers citing OpenEvidence's fast-growing pharma advertising business; a securities suit (10-Q legal note) alleges Doximity was 'losing market share to competitors with more favorable pricing and engagement models'.
key_numbers: P/E 27.9 vs 52.3 own median; P/FCF 17.2 vs 39.9; FCF-SBC yield 3.6%; NRR 103% (118% a year ago); Q2 FY27 rev +4%; adj. EBITDA margin 51% vs 60%; ~$713M cash and securities, no debt
